observation.visible_scene: A bonfire burns at dusk on a grassy clearing bordered by dark, leafy trees. The fire sits atop a bed of glowing embers and is fed by a teepee-like arrangement of dry branches and twigs, with a larger loose pile of cut branches stacked to the right of the flames. The camera is stationary throughout; the tree trunks, the branch pile, and the grass foreground hold fixed positions across every frame.
visible_changes: The flames continuously flicker, changing height and shape frame by frame: at times short and broad (e.g. frames 1, 3, 7, 23), at times tall and narrow with a pointed tip (e.g. frames 5, 35, 41). This is deformation of the flame plume, not movement of an object.
The bright yellow-white base of the fire stays roughly constant in position and intensity, while the orange-red flame tips above it rise, lean, and split.
A faint dark smoke plume rises above the flames against the trees, drifting and thinning as it ascends.
The ember bed at the base glows steadily with small localized bright spots that flicker.
The branch structure (left twigs and right pile) shows no positional change; only the lighting on it shifts slightly with the flame flicker.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the fire was started and what fuel it contains beyond the visible branches.
Whether the fire grows, peaks, or dies down after the excerpt ends.
The presence or direction of wind driving the flicker.
uncertain_details: The exact cause of the flame shape changes (airflow vs. fuel) is not observable.
Minor camera drift cannot be fully ruled out, but background landmarks appear fixed, so the scene is treated as static-camera.
